Speeds up the two CI jobs that each took over 10 minutes: **Backend — tests** and **Frontend — browser E2E**.

## Backend — tests: parallel with pytest-xdist
- `pytest-xdist==3.8.0` (MIT; its one dependency, execnet, is MIT) in `backend/requirements-dev.txt`. CI runs `pytest backend/tests/ -n 4 --dist loadfile`: four workers, one per runner core, and a test file never splits across workers, so the probe databases and roles a file creates by fixed name never meet another worker's.
- `backend/tests/conftest.py`: each worker gets its own database (`<name>_gwN`, created through the server's `postgres` DB) and its own Redis index. A serial run is unchanged.
- `structlog.configure` is wrapped so tests never cache loggers. Cached loggers hid lines from `capture_logs` depending on which test ran first (26 files use it).
- Checkout uses `filter: blob:none` (it took 64 s with `fetch-depth: 0`); the upgrade-path gate still has every commit and tag.

Two tests depended on running alone:
- `test_trigger_labels.py`: `uuid4()` parametrize ids made each worker collect a different test list, which xdist refuses.
- `test_secrets.py::test_approle_403_relogin_is_compare_and_swap_under_concurrency`: the fake refused every token, so the login count tracked thread scheduling. Now only the cached token is revoked and the test asserts `logins == 2`. **Mutation-checked:** with an unconditional clear in `_forget_token_if_current` it fails 3/3 (8–9 logins for 8 threads).

The parallel runs also surfaced two ordering bugs, fixed in their own PRs: #2768 (a product bug: the rollup sweep's `LIMIT … SKIP LOCKED` claim could take past its batch size) and #2769 (planner tests that a unique rival index could win).

**Local timings** (same machine, `--no-cov`): serial 348 s → `-n 4` **~87 s**. Three consecutive `-n 4` runs after merging `main`: 10515 passed, 178 skipped (the opt-in live lanes), 0 failed, 86–88 s each. CI's serial `pytest` took 677 s in run 46059360413; this PR's run gives the CI number.

## Frontend — browser E2E: the static demo gets its own job
- New job **`frontend-demo`** ("Frontend — static demo (record, build, smoke)") runs the demo record/build/smoke (322 s of the E2E job's time) in parallel with the Playwright specs. It shares the E2E job's services, env and setup steps through YAML anchors, the repo's first. This PR's CI run is what proves the runner accepts them.
- `publish-demo` now `needs: frontend-demo`. Required check names are unchanged.

Not done here: splitting the demo's 69-route walk across pages. The job is now off the critical path, so it waits on measured numbers from this PR's run.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

content.content:
---
title: API versions
url: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/versioning
description: "When making API requests, you must send an `anthropic-version` request header. For example, `anthropic-version: 2026-10-21`. If you are using the [client SDK](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/cli-sdks-libraries/overview), it sets this header for you."
---

For any given API version, Anthropic preserves:

* Existing input parameters
* Existing output parameters

However, Anthropic may do the following:

* Add additional optional inputs
* Add additional values to the output
* Change conditions for specific error types
* Add new variants to enum-like output values (for example, streaming event types)

Generally, if you are using the API as documented in this reference, Anthropic will not break your usage.

## Version history

Anthropic recommends using the latest API version whenever possible.

* `2026-10-21`

  * [Migrating to API version 2026-10-21](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21) shows how to upgrade.

  * Available on the Claude API, [Claude Platform on AWS](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-platform-on-aws), [Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-models-on-google-cloud/anthropic-managed), [Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed)](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-models-on-google-cloud/google-managed), and [Microsoft Foundry](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/claude-in-microsoft-foundry). On Amazon Bedrock, it’s available for Claude 4.7 and later models. For earlier Claude models on Bedrock, [keep the API version that you use today](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/migration-2026-10-21#availability).

  * Messages API:

    * A request that places a `document` block directly in an `assistant` message returns a 400 error.
    * Sending a `text` block with a non-empty `citations` array in a `user` message, directly or inside a `search_result` block, returns a 400 error.
    * The `temperature`, `top_p`, and `top_k` request parameters are removed. A request that sends any of them returns a 400 error on every model.

  * Admin API:

    * [RBAC groups](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/rbac_groups/list) no longer return `roles`. Use `role_ids` instead.
    * [RBAC group members](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/rbac_groups/members/list), and the response to removing one, no longer return `group_id`. Use `rbac_group_id` instead.
    * [RBAC roles](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/rbac_roles/list) no longer return `name`. Use `display_name` instead.
    * [Organization](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/organization/rate_limits/list) and [workspace](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/organization/workspaces/rate_limits/list) rate-limit entries, and the response to [setting a workspace’s rate limits](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/organization/workspaces/rate_limits/update), no longer return `group_type`. Use `group.type` instead.
    * [API keys](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/organization/api_keys/list) no longer return `workspace_id`. Use `scope.workspace_id` instead. It holds the ID of the key’s workspace, the Default Workspace included. An all-workspaces key has no `scope.workspace_id`.

  * Claude Enterprise Analytics API:

    * The per-user [usage](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/analytics/user_usage_report/list) and [cost](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/beta/organization/analytics/user_cost_report/list) reports no longer have `actor.email`. Use `actor.email_address` instead.

For any given API version, Anthropic preserves:

* Existing input parameters
* Existing output parameters

However, Anthropic may do the following:

* Add additional optional inputs
* Add additional values to the output
* Change conditions for specific error types

gh pr create --base main --head test/issue-2766-cross-browser-owner-picker --milestone "v1.3 Week 8 — test & dependency debt, decisions & cycle close" --label no-changelog --title "test(e2e): press Enter in the owner picker only once an option is active" --body "Fixes #2766

## Cause
Enter in rc-select picks the **active** option. \`@rc-component/select\` 1.12 marks the first option active in a \`useEffect\` keyed on the option count (\`OptionList.js\`, \"Auto active first item when list length or searchValue changed\"), so there is a render where the option is visible but not yet active. The transfer spec pressed Enter as soon as \`getByText(ANALYST)\` was visible, inside that window. Firefox and WebKit land there more often, so nothing was picked and **Transfer** stayed disabled.

**App or spec?** The spec. A keyboard user reads the result and then presses Enter; the effect has run long before a person can react. So this isn't an accessibility defect.

## Fix
- Both owner-picker specs (transfer, and offboarding's heir picker) wait for \`.ant-select-item-option-active\` with the user's text before pressing Enter.
- The transfer spec asserts **Transfer** is enabled before clicking it, so a miss fails with a clear message instead of a click timeout.

## Evidence
Dispatched the full CI with the weekly lane on this branch: run [46110974530](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/actions/runs/46110974530). \`Playwright E2E\` (Chromium), **\`Cross-browser E2E (Firefox, WebKit)\`** and the OTP lane all passed.

The two WebKit flakes from the issue (\`check-editor.spec.ts:113\`, \`suites.spec.ts:58\`) passed in that run with no change. They passed on retry in the first run too. If they come back on a Monday run, they get their own issue with that run's trace.

from backend.tests.support.migrations import load_migration

_MIGRATION_PATH = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "alembic" / "versions" / "c4e5a6b7d8f9_add_incidents.py"
)


def _load_migration() -> Any:
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("_incidents_migration", _MIGRATION_PATH)
    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def _has_incidents(connection: Any) -> bool:
    return bool(inspect(connection).has_table("incidents"))

def test_downgrade_narrows_and_upgrade_widens_both_value_sets(db_session: Any) -> None:
    db = db_session
    module = load_migration(_FILE)
    assert "'suite'" in _provider_check(db)
    assert "suite:%" in _dedup_predicate(db)

    ctx = MigrationContext.configure(db.connection(), opts={"target_metadata": Base.metadata})
    with Operations.context(ctx):
        module._set_provider_check(module._NO_SUITE)
    _rebuild_index(db, module, module._DEDUP_NO_SUITE)
